entities.summary:
Cináed mac Írgalaig, also known as Cináed Cáech, 'the one-eyed', was an Irish King of Brega who ruled from approximately 725 to 728 CE. He was High King of Ireland and a powerful leader in the medieval period.

Cináed mac Írgalaig was born around 700 CE, and his reign was marked by significant events, including the establishment of a strong kingdom in Brega and his efforts to consolidate power in Ireland. He was known for his military campaigns and his ability to unite the various Irish kingdoms under his rule.

Despite his significance, Cináed mac Írgalaig's legacy is somewhat overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, such as the Viking invasions of Ireland and the rise of the Uí Néill dynasty. Nevertheless, his reign marked an important period in Irish history, and he remains a significant figure in the annals of medieval Irish monarchy.

Cináed mac Írgalaig's legacy can be seen in the many place names and cultural artifacts that bear his name, including the town of Brega in County Leitrim, Ireland. His impact on Irish history and culture continues to be felt today, making him a vital figure in the study of medieval Irish society.

Cináed mac Írgalaig, also known as Cináed Cáech, 'the one-eyed', was an Irish King of Brega who served as High King of Ireland from 665 CE to 728 CE.

    He played a pivotal role in the power struggles of the medieval Irish kingdoms, navigating the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various factions.

    One of his most notable achievements was his successful campaign against the Viking invasions of Ireland, which he repelled with the help of his trusted advisor, Dál Riata.

    Despite his military prowess, Cináed mac Írgalaig's legacy is also marked by controversy, as he was known for his brutal suppression of dissent and his role in the forced conversion of the Picts to Christianity.

    His impact can still be felt in modern-day Ireland, where he is remembered as a powerful and enigmatic figure, whose name has become synonymous with the complexities and challenges of Irish history.
